text:
oliver: FYI security plans to tighten the keystore firewall in eu-west-2 at 03:00 UTC tomorrow. They called out privatelink endpoints being moved to a deny-by-default ACL.
infra-bot: Change scheduled by @security: CHG-20241201-301, action: keystore-firewall-tighten-euw2, window 2024-12-01T03:00Z.
rachel: Which onboarding traffic will break? our warmpool nodes hit keystore via privatelink from 10.21.48.0/22 and the spot-onboarders from 10.21.52.0/24.
sam: Those subnets aren't in the allowlist currently. If ACL blocks them we'll see handshake failures and onboarding retries. Last time this caused ~25% slower effective capacity.
kevin: Cost impact estimate: longer warmup = more instance-hours for the prep fleet + increased spot churn. Back-of-envelope 7-10% uplift for the AZ for the 3-4h window.
oliver: Mitigation idea: add short-lived allowlist entries for onboarding subnets, gate via tf toggle, run a 3-node canary that performs full join flows, and watch error metrics. Rollback ACL if canary fails.
rachel: Agree. Also suggest lowering kube readiness retry threshold so failed handshakes fail fast instead of stalling. Change readiness to fail after 4 failed attempts (was 12).
sam: I'll author a tiny TF change with a TTL tag. Plan: add tag `temp-allow:euw2-warmpool` with expiry timestamp and rollback script.
kevin: Monitoring: create alarm on keystore 5xx > 2% for 5m, and onboarding duration > baseline + 15% for 10m. Tie to PD escalation if both fire.
infra-bot: Temporary incident channel created: #temp/keystore-euw2-firewall-canary.
oliver: Can we test the privatelink handshake beforehand? quick curl that hits keystore-proxy and returns status: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "X-Node: warmpool-canary" https://keystore-proxy.internal/handshake` should be 200.
rachel: I'll run a preflight at 02:30 UTC. If we see 403 then we abort the planned allowlist change and ask security to exclude the privatelink IP range.
sam: PR incoming: branch `temp/keystore-euw2-allowlist`, PR -> https://git.company/infra/pull/811. TFvar `allowlist_ttl = "4h"` included.
kevin: Also add an autoscaler safety: pause large-scale warmups if onboarding latency > 2x baseline for 15m. That prevents us from spinning up excessive prep capacity.
oliver: Good call. Who owns the rollback? I'll hold the change and will be primary for rollback with one click revert to previous ACL.
rachel: I'll update the kube readiness config PR and link it to the canary run.
sam: Canary runbook: 1) apply temp allowlist 2) deploy 3-node canary warmpool with image tag `gpu-onboard:canary-20241201` 3) run handshake curl test 4) monitor metrics for 15m 5) promote or rollback.
kevin: Tagging cost-ops: if cost > threshold alert and we will hold further onboarding.
oliver: Schedule: preflight 02:30, apply allowlist 02:45, canary 02:50, monitor till 03:05, then proceed with full ACL change at 03:00 (security will still apply; we coordinate). Slight overlap possible but can abort.
rachel: One more safety: add a fallback route in kube join process to use `keystore-fallback.shared` (other AZ endpoint) if handshake fails with status 403. That reduces total outage surface.
sam: I added a short circuit in the join code to attempt fallback once before retrying. Will roll with canary image.
kevin: All alarms created, PD runbook linked.
oliver: Thanks. Please be on-call 02:20-03:30 UTC. Post-run we'll debrief and decide whether a permanent keystore peering for onboarding is warranted.
infra-bot: Change CHG-20241201-301 confirmed; watchers: oliver, rachel, sam, kevin.
